title: Unique identifier linking health logs to individuals
description: Health log store contains user identifiers that link calorie intake, weight history, and exercise session data to specific individuals, enabling data linkage across the system.
assumptions: Health logs include user identification information

title: Profiling individuals through health data patterns
description: Stored health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) can be analyzed to create detailed profiles of individuals' health behaviors and patterns.
assumptions: Health data is stored with sufficient granularity for pattern analysis

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The companion mobile app processes identified personal health data including calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions.
assumptions: App processes data with user identification

title: Quasi-identifier combinations in health logs
description: Combinations of health attributes (weight history, exercise frequency, calorie patterns) could serve as quasi-identifiers to identify individuals even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Health data contains multiple attributes that could uniquely identify individuals

title: Health data as attributable evidence
description: Stored health logs can be used to attribute specific health behaviors and activities to individuals, preventing them from denying certain claims about their health data.
assumptions: Health logs are stored with sufficient detail to attribute actions to users

title: Sensitive health data types collected
description: Health logs contain highly sensitive personal data (weight history, calorie intake, exercise sessions) that requires strict protection and justification for collection.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Health data retention duration
description: Health logs may be stored longer than functionally necessary, creating unnecessary privacy risks from prolonged data retention.
assumptions: Retention policies may not be clearly defined or limited to functional needs

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data (calorie intake, weight, exercise) is being collected, processed, and stored in the health log store.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain health data processing

title: Lack of control over health data rectification and erasure
description: Users may lack adequate controls to correct inaccurate health data or delete their health logs from the data store.
assumptions: Data subject rights implementation may be incomplete

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Collection of detailed health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) may exceed what is functionally necessary for the app's purpose.
assumptions: All collected health data types may not be strictly required

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Health data may be stored longer than necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Retention periods may not be clearly defined or enforced

title: Health profiling through cross-session analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service analyzes calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions to perform health-condition analysis. This enables profiling of individuals based on their health data patterns, linking data points to create comprehensive health profiles.
assumptions: Health logs contain sufficient data points across sessions to enable meaningful profiling

title: Quasi-identifier identification through health data patterns
description: Health data (calorie intake, weight, exercise patterns) across sessions can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify individuals, especially when combined with temporal patterns.
assumptions: Health data patterns are sufficiently unique to individuals

title: Sensitive health data collection
description: Health logs containing calorie, weight, and exercise data are highly sensitive personal data types. Processing this data for health-condition analysis requires careful justification of necessity.
assumptions: Health data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations

title: Excessive volume of health data processing
description: Reading health logs 'across sessions' suggests processing of historical data beyond what may be functionally needed for current health-condition analysis, potentially violating data minimization.
assumptions: Not all historical session data is required for the analytics function
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether all historical data is actually needed

title: Unawareness of health data analytics processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed across sessions for health-condition analysis, particularly if this processing occurs without explicit notification.
assumptions: Users are not explicitly informed about cross-session health analytics

title: Lack of control over health data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their health data is processed for analytics, including which data types are analyzed and for what purposes.
assumptions: No user preference mechanism exists for health analytics processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing health logs across all sessions for health-condition analysis may process more personal data than is actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulation applies to this health data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific regulatory context and whether all session data is truly necessary

title: Lawfulness concerns for sensitive health data processing
description: Health data is sensitive personal data requiring specific lawful grounds for processing. Automated health-condition analysis may raise additional lawfulness concerns under regulations like GDPR.
assumptions: Health data qualifies as sensitive personal data under applicable law
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific regulatory framework and lawful basis established

title: Profiling through location pattern analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history across sessions, enabling profiling of individuals based on their behavioral patterns and location data.
assumptions: Location history contains sufficient temporal and spatial detail to enable meaningful pattern analysis

title: Location history as quasi-identifier
description: Location history across multiple sessions can serve as a quasi-identifier that uniquely identifies individuals, as movement patterns are often distinctive to specific persons.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity and temporal coverage to enable re-identification

title: Excessive analysis and pattern derivation
description: The analytics service performs treatment, analysis, and enrichment of location data to derive movement patterns and daily routines, which may exceed what is functionally necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Pattern derivation goes beyond basic analytics to infer behavioral characteristics

title: Extended retention of location history
description: Location history is stored across multiple sessions, indicating long-term retention that may exceed what is functionally necessary for the analytics purpose.
assumptions: Location history is retained beyond the immediate session or short-term analysis needs

title: Unawareness of pattern analysis
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, beyond simple location tracking.
assumptions: Users consent to location tracking but may not understand the extent of pattern analysis

title: Lack of control over pattern processing
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their location data is processed for pattern analysis, including the ability to set preferences or consent to specific types of analysis.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism exists for different types of location analytics

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history across sessions to derive movement patterns may process more personal data than is actually needed for the functional purpose of health analytics.
assumptions: The stated purpose could be achieved with less extensive location data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific health analytics requirements and whether pattern analysis is truly necessary

title: Health profiling through analytics insights
description: The Health Analytics Service creates and returns health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that profile individuals based on their health data patterns. This enables linking of data to specific individuals through behavioral and health pattern analysis.
assumptions: The analytics service processes individual health data to generate personalized insights

title: Revealing health attributes in analytics output
description: Health-condition risk indicators and trend flags contain revealing attributes that can identify or distinguish data subjects. Health data is inherently sensitive and can be used to identify individuals even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Health analytics outputs contain attributes that can distinguish individuals

title: Sensitive health data types disclosed
description: Health-condition risk indicators are highly sensitive personal data types. The disclosure of such data to the mobile app may exceed what is functionally required, especially if the app does not need all risk indicators for its core functionality.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Unnecessary enrichment of health data
description: The analytics service performs treatment, analysis, and enrichment of health data to generate inferred insights (risk indicators, trend flags) that may not be strictly necessary for the app's functionality. This represents additional processing beyond raw data transmission.
assumptions: The inferred insights represent enrichment beyond what the app functionally requires

title: User unawareness of health insight generation
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health data is being analyzed to generate risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags. The inferred nature of these insights may not be transparent to users.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of analytics processing on their health data

title: Lack of control over health analytics preferences
description: Users may lack control over what health insights are generated and shared with the app. They may not be able to set preferences or consent to specific types of health analytics processing.
assumptions: The system does not provide granular consent controls for different types of health analytics

title: Automated decision making on sensitive health data
description: The generation of health-condition risk indicators and trend flags constitutes automated processing of sensitive health data. This may require specific lawful grounds and safeguards under GDPR and similar regulations.
assumptions: Health data is classified as special category data requiring enhanced protection
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific regulatory framework and whether risk indicators constitute automated decision-making

title: Sensitive health data disclosed to user
description: The app displays highly sensitive health-related data including eating-disorder and diabetes risk signals. While this is intended for the user, the processing and display of such sensitive health indicators represents a data disclosure of highly sensitive personal data types.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are considered sensitive personal data under most privacy frameworks

title: Inferred health conditions processed beyond functional necessity
description: The app processes and displays inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) through analysis and transformation of user data. This enrichment and inference processing may exceed what is functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The inference of health conditions represents additional processing beyond basic data display

title: Limited user control over health data processing preferences
description: Users may lack control over which health indicators are inferred and displayed, or how their personal data is processed to generate these risk signals. The app may not provide granular consent or preference settings for sensitive health data processing.
assumptions: The app may not offer detailed user preferences for health data processing
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether the app provides preference controls for health data processing

title: Processing of sensitive health data may lack proper lawful basis
description: The processing of sensitive health data (eating-disorder and diabetes risk indicators) requires specific lawful grounds under regulations like GDPR. Automated decision-making on sensitive health data has additional legal requirements that may not be met.
assumptions: Health risk indicators qualify as sensitive personal data requiring special protection
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific legal framework and consent mechanisms in place

title: Revealing health attributes enable identification
description: The health risk indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes signals) are highly revealing attributes that could support identification of the data subject, especially when combined with other data or in contexts where such conditions are rare.
assumptions: Health conditions can serve as identifying attributes in certain contexts

title: Highly sensitive health data disclosed to third-party cloud provider
description: The full health and location dataset is being hosted and replicated at a third-party cloud provider. Health data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly necessary for the system's functionality.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive personal data under most privacy regulations

title: Personal data exposed to predetermined external party
description: Health and location data is made accessible to the cloud hosting provider (EE2), which is a predetermined external party. This increases the number of parties with access to sensitive personal data beyond the original health analytics service.
assumptions: The cloud provider is a known third-party at design time

title: Excessive volume of personal data processed
description: The 'full health and location dataset' is being replicated at the cloud provider, suggesting an excessive amount of personal data is being processed beyond what might be functionally needed for analytics purposes.
assumptions: Full dataset replication may exceed functional requirements

title: Quasi-identifiers in health and location data
description: The combination of health data and location data can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow identification of data subjects, especially when combined with other available information.
assumptions: Health and location data combinations can uniquely identify individuals

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Health and location data at the cloud provider can be combined to create quasi-identifiers that enable linking of data to specific individuals across different datasets or contexts.
assumptions: Data at cloud provider can be combined with other data sources

title: Data subjects unaware of third-party data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health and location data is being hosted and replicated at a third-party cloud provider, especially if this is not clearly disclosed in privacy notices.
assumptions: Third-party data sharing may not be transparently communicated to data subjects

title: Lack of control over data rectification and erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification or erasure of their health and location data stored at the third-party cloud provider, as the data is replicated and may be difficult to fully remove.
assumptions: Data replication at cloud provider complicates data subject rights enforcement

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Replicating the full health and location dataset at a third-party cloud provider may violate the data minimization principle if the full dataset is not strictly necessary for the analytics functionality.
assumptions: Full dataset replication may exceed what is functionally required
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific analytics requirements and data processing agreements

title: Lawfulness concerns for health data processing
description: Processing of health data (special category data) at a third-party cloud provider requires specific lawful grounds and appropriate safeguards. Without proper data processing agreements and security measures, this may constitute unlawful processing.
assumptions: Health data requires special legal protections under GDPR and similar regulations
uncertainty_note: Depends on existence of proper DPAs and security measures
